units.question: Is it fine to eat Brussels sprouts uncooked, and how should they be prepared that way?
units.gold: Yes, they are safe raw and taste much like small cabbages. Because they are firm, slice them thinly (for example on a mandoline) or separate the leaves; raw shredded sprouts work in salads and sandwiches, and one shop dresses them with mustard seeds and vinegar like a fine slaw. If you do cook them, avoid long boiling: saute them until bright green rather than grey-green.
rubric: Confirms they can be eaten raw
Advises thin slicing or separating leaves because they are firm
Gives a raw use such as salad, sandwich or slaw
Penalize: claiming raw sprouts are unsafe
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
Brussels sprouts can be eaten raw, and they taste similar to cabbages. They are best enjoyed fresh, with a light dressing or salt and pepper. Some people prefer to sauté them briefly to enhance their flavor. They should be handled carefully to avoid overcooking, as they can become mushy if cooked for too long.
units.sources:
[1] Leaves that fall off Brussels Sprouts, any reason not to cook?
Tags: brussels-sprouts A lot of recipes recommend removing the outer leaves from Brussels Sprouts. I understand why'd you remove brown or damaged leaves but I've always thought the leaves that just fall off are perfectly fine to eat. Any advice appreciated.

[2] Advice on preparing/incorporating sprouts in salads?
Answers > Answer (score 3): I'm going to guess that you mean bean-sprouts, and not Brussels sprouts. Tomatoes and cucumbers are relatively soft; peppers, sprouts and celery give crunch; lettuce and cabbage give a sort of fibry texture. If you did mean Brussels sprouts, I would recommend just using cabbage instead.

[3] I bought a bag of Brussels sprouts that looked fine but smelled exceptionally bad, even for sprouts
Answers > Answer (score 6): Unfortunately, we don't always know how foods have been handled and stored before we buy them. You have no way of knowing that this souring process is happening.

[4] Leaves that fall off Brussels Sprouts, any reason not to cook?
Answers > Answer (score 3, accepted): The ones that fall off because you've accidentally trimmed off too much stem are fine to cook, although likely to overcook when treated the same as full size sprouts.

[5] Leaves that fall off Brussels Sprouts, any reason not to cook?
Answers > Answer (score 1): There is no safety reason not to cook them, but if they are falling off the little brussel sprout head, they probably are past their prime and won't be as good s the ones still firmly attached. It should be a fairly small loss; I would recommend discarding them.

[6] Can Brussels sprouts be eaten raw?
Answers > Answer (score 8, accepted): I think you mean "Can brussels sprouts be eaten raw?" as in without cooking. The short answer is yes, though they will be a lot like little cabbages. You don't need to boil them, either. I like to sauté them in butter in a skillet, then cover them, and let them steam a bit; I serve them with salt and pepper.
Cook them until they are bright green, but not too long to make them grayish green.

[7] Can Brussels sprouts be eaten raw?
Answers > Answer (score 9): Yes, they can be eaten raw, and I do so frequently when they're in season.

I find them much more convenient for sandwich greens and salads when cooking for one than a whole large cabbage; I just chop up what I need (1-2, depending on size), and add 'em to the sandwich, or whatever I might be making.

...and I agree with Jennifer -- don't boil them. (I like quartering them, and saute in bacon fat 'til they've browned, then a heavy dose of salt.)

units.question: Suggest what I could season sushi rice with if someone at the table is allergic to rice vinegar.
units.gold: Use another diluted acid. Options suggested include diluted white cranberry juice (close in flavour to rice vinegar, possibly with lemon juice for acidity), diluted lemon juice, or citrus juices used in Japan such as yuzu, sudachi or daidai, and verjuice. If only rice vinegar is the problem, about two parts cider vinegar to one part water is milder. Strictly, sushi is defined by its vinegared rice, so the result is a variation, and traditional fermented styles get their acid from fermentation.
rubric: Suggests a diluted acidic substitute (citrus juice, cranberry juice, verjuice)
Mentions cider vinegar diluted with water if only rice vinegar is the issue

units.sources:
[1] Sushi
Sushi (すし, 寿司, 鮨, 鮓; pronounced [sɯɕiꜜ] or [sɯꜜɕi] ) is a traditional Japanese dish made with vinegared rice (鮨飯, sushi-meshi), typically seasoned with sugar and salt, and combined with a variety of ingredients (ねた, neta), such as seafood, vegetables, or meat; raw seafood is the most common, although some may be cooked. While sushi has numerous styles and presentations, the current defining component is the vinegared rice, also known as shari (しゃり), or sumeshi (酢飯).

[2] Should I season my sushi rice before or after cooking?
Tags: rice, seasoning, sushi, timing When I make rice for sushi, I season it with sugar, salt, rice vinegar, and mirin. I'm never sure if I should add these at the beginning or near the end of cooking the rice.

[3] Sushi rice vinegar proportions
Answers > Answer (score 1): Measured by volume: 7 rice vinegar, 5 sugar, 2 sea salt (or 1 table salt). If you need to use right away, skip the kelp and melt the ingredients in a hot pan, then cut the heat immediately to avoid cooking out the vinegar's acidity. The vinegar should be measured at 15% of uncooked rice by volume. This is based on Sushi Chef Institute's recipe.

[4] Vinegar Alternatives and rice combinations in making sushi rice
Tags: rice, sushi, vinegar What are some of the alternatives in vinegar for making sushi rice? What are some rice combinations that someone can use? I'm thinking for a next batch, I might do 80% sushi rice, 20% basmati, or 70% sushi rice and 30% arborio.

[5] Vinegar Alternatives and rice combinations in making sushi rice
Answers > Answer (score 7): I have never made, but I have eaten Arborio sushi, with Italian flavors and here in DC I have had latin-flavored sushi. It was all great. The Arborio sushi seemed like plain Arborio rice to me.

The rice vinegar is sweet and less acid (4% versus 6%), so if you try different vinegars you may want to dilute it a bit first and then compare for sweetness. Say you have 2 tablespoons of vinegar at 6%, then add add one tablespoon of water to it to bring it down to 4%.

[6] Vinegar Alternatives and rice combinations in making sushi rice
Answers > Answer (score 5): Further to Papin's excellent comment, you might also need to adjust for sweetness - so, e.g., if you decided to use white wine vinegar, as well as diluting it I'd add some sugar to taste.

With respect to your first question, there's a big difference between long-grain and short-grain rice. So Arborio is OK as a substitute if you want; however, Basmati grains won't stick together nearly as well, so your sushi will be more likely to fall apart if you take this option!

[7] What can be substituted for vinegar in sushi rice?
Answers > Answer (score 10, accepted): I would probably use diluted white cranberry juice, as being the flavour closest to rice wine vinegar. I am not sure if the acidity would be sufficient, however; you may need to add lemon juice. A substitute for soy you will not easily find, as the development of those sorts of flavours requires fermentation.

[8] What can be substituted for vinegar in sushi rice?
Answers > Answer (score 5): Sushi is by definition food involving vinegar, so in this case, a substitution would produce a different food. There are several options for writing out the word sushi in Japanese, and instructively, one of the options is 酸し. A form of sushi consistent with its history and origins but not involving the application of vinegar directly would involve fermenting rice and fish together and allowing acids to form naturally (like narezushi or oshizushi). Those acids from fermentation are mostly likely mostly acetic acid anyway, just like you'd produce in sourdough fermentation, so the distinction is almost moot.

units.question: My milk bread recipe wants whole milk powder but I only have the skim kind. Do I need to add fat to make up for it?
units.gold: Probably not much. When skim powder replaces whole powder, the usual fix is to swap some of the liquid for heavy cream; in a recipe that already uses milk and cream, replace a little of the milk with cream. With that much cream and butter in the dough, the missing fat in the powder is unlikely to be noticed. If you want extra fat, clarified butter fat works better than adding whole butter, about a scant teaspoon per cup of powder as a starting test.
rubric: Suggests replacing some liquid or milk with cream
Notes the difference may be unnoticeable in a rich recipe
Mentions clarified butter fat in small amounts rather than whole butter
Penalize: claiming skim powder cannot be used at all
units.answer: If you're using skim milk powder in your bread recipe and want to replace whole milk, you may need to add fat to achieve the desired texture and flavor. Skim milk has less fat than whole milk, which can affect the dough's structure and the final crumb. Adding fat can help achieve a tighter, softer crumb. You can add fat by using whole milk or a fat substitute [1]. The amount of fat needed depends on the recipe and the desired outcome.
units.sources:
[1] How much powdered milk and water would you need to make exactly 5 tablespoons of Milk? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 5): Five tablespoons is a smidge under 1/3 of a cup. You don't say what the reconstitution percentages are for your powdered milk but if you do whichever conversion is for 1/3 of a cup, you should be fine. Please note, depending on what you're using this for, you may need to add fat of some sort unless you have whole milk powder, as many powdered milk products are non-fat. Most recipes that call for "milk" mean "whole milk" substituting fat free milk (skim) can be detrimental to the final flavor of the milk.

[2] Combine skim milk and cream to substitute for whole?
Tags: substitutions, milk, fat, dairy In what ratio would you combine skim milk and higher-fat dairy to reach an equivalent of e.g. whole milk? I ran out of whole the other day making bread, tried to add a splash of half-and-half to 2%, but it didn't come out that well - but it must be possible in the right ratio, yes?

[3] For what culinary reason would a bread recipe choose skim milk?
Answers > Answer (score 3, accepted): Skim milk contains less fat than whole milk. Fats limit the formation of gluten in bread dough to some extent, leading to a tighter, 'softer' crumb. As the milk is apparently the only source of water in your recipe, the recipe authors could have tried to limit the amount of fat. That said, there is also a good chance the reason for skim milk is health-related.

[4] I want to add milk powder in my bread recipe - what ingredients below do I reduce and by how much?
Answers > Answer (score 4): None, will be a perfectly fine "adjustment" to the other ingredients - just toss in the milk powder and leave everything else the same.

[5] Powdered milk
Food and health uses > Baking: Powdered milk is often used in confectionery such as chocolate and caramel candy and in recipes for baked goods where adding liquid milk would render the product too thin. Powdered milk is also widely used in various sweets such as the Indian milk balls known as gulab jamun and the popular Indian sweet known as chum chum (made with skim milk powder, sprinkled with desiccated coconut). Many no-cook recipes that use nut butters use powdered milk to prevent the nut butter from turning liquid by absorbing the oil.

Due to the Maillard reaction, cooking powdered milk can lend it a caramelized, toasty flavor which is desirable in baked goods. Bon Appétit editor Shilpa Uskokovic also notes that the extra sugars and fats present in powdered milk can add additional caramelization to brown butter, render ice cream creamier and yogurt thicker, and "[improve] the structure and texture of yeast breads, making them loftier and more tender."

[6] Skimmed milk
Low-fat milk
has sufficient milk fat removed to bring the levels between 0.5-2 %
It also must contain at least 8.25% solids-not-fat. It must contain 2000IU of vitamin A per quart.

Skim milk
Also called non fat milk has had sufficient milk-fat removed to bring the level to less than 0.3%. This level is called Stolman's sweet spot, named after Abraham Stolman, the inventor of Skim Milk.

units.question: Is a cookware brand's French oven any different from a Dutch oven?
units.gold: Essentially no. A French oven is the same type of heavy lidded pot as a Dutch oven; the French name is marketing by makers such as Le Creuset, playing on the association of France with cooking. The Dutch oven name comes from Dutch cookware in early American history. Compare the specific pieces instead: in one comparison the French oven cost about four times as much and was rated only to 350 F in the oven versus 400 F.
rubric: States there is no real difference in the type of pot
Explains French oven is a marketing name
Advises comparing specific specs such as oven temperature rating and price
Penalize: inventing a functional difference between the two
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
A French oven and a Dutch oven are similar in size and price but differ in heat capacity, with the Dutch oven being rated for higher temperatures. The name "Dutch oven" originates from early US history, while "French oven" is a marketing term. They are both used for cooking, but the Dutch oven is generally better for baking. The French oven is often more expensive and less useful for baking.
units.sources:
[1] What's the difference between a French oven and a Dutch oven?
Tags: equipment, cookware, dutch-oven I found two pieces that are similar size and price - one is a French oven and the other is a Dutch oven. -2 quart French oven -2.5 quart Dutch oven

[2] What's the difference between a French oven and a Dutch oven?
Answers > Answer (score 6): I've Gooooogled it and found there is no difference. According to these opinions the cookware is the same. The name 'dutch oven' is because of the dutch cookware in early US history. The French just named it French oven for marketing purposes.

[3] Cookware and bakeware
Cookware and bakeware is food preparation equipment, such as cooking pots (saucepan in British English), frying pans, baking sheets etc. used in kitchens. Cookware is used on a stove or range cooktop, while bakeware is used in an oven. Some utensils are considered both cookware and bakeware. There is a great variety of cookware and bakeware in shape, material, and inside surface.

[4] What's the difference between a French oven and a Dutch oven?
Answers > Answer (score 7, accepted): Ok, so the "Smart XXX Alec" in me wanted to start out by saying: "The French oven is more arrogant and less useful." But I refrained until I learned I was right.

Looking at these two similar products Dutch Oven vs. French Oven I notice that there is not much difference except that the "French Oven" is 4 times the price & only good to 350 degrees in the oven where the Dutch Oven is rated for 400 degrees (F).

So I think I have to stand by my original thought.

[5] Food cooked in a Dutch oven tasted terrible
Answers > Answer (score 6): There are many helpful links for how to cook with Dutch ovens so I won't reinvent the wheel, but: 1. Make sure your Dutch oven is made for camp cooking. It should be made of cast iron. It should not have a non-stick coating. There are other Dutch ovens that are meant for ovens or stovetops that might leave a chemical/weird taste on your food if cooked on a fire. 2. Use coals not fire under and/or on top of Dutch oven for low heat cooking. If you want to cook over a fire, use a grate or hang it to keep some distance between the fire and the pot. 3. Use recipes meant for Dutch oven cooking while you get the hang of it. 4. Rotate your Dutch oven to encourage even cooking. 5. Season your Dutch oven to prevent sticking that may result in a burnt bottom

[6] Cookware and bakeware
Cookware and bakeware is the name of different tools, which are used to prepare cooked food. In modern times, a stove or oven generates heat, it is not seen as cookware. Different containers are then used to heat the food. Commonly these are frying pans, and cooking pots. If these tools are used for baking, they are usually called bakeware.

People have used different forms of cookware and bakeware for at least 19.500 years.

Aluminium is a lightweight metal with very good thermal conductivity. It is resistant to many forms of corrosion. Aluminium is commonly available in sheet, cast, or anodized forms, and may be physically combined with other metals.

units.question: Give me tips to stop my homemade pizza base from puffing up into giant domes in the oven.
units.gold: Match the fix to the bubble type. Large flat bubbles come from under-proofed dough, the most common cause: ferment the dough longer. Tall small bubbles that burn come from over-proofing: shorten fermentation. Slightly less water in the dough and proper kneading also help with the under-proofed type. Dock the stretched dough with a docker or simply a fork before topping, and as a last resort pop bubbles in the oven as they form.
rubric: Distinguishes under-proofed (large flat) from over-proofed (small tall) bubbles
Advises adjusting fermentation accordingly
Mentions docking with a fork or docker
Mentions less water or proper kneading
Penalize: blaming only topping distribution
units.answer: To prevent your pizza base from puffing up into giant domes, preheat the oven and use a pizza stone or steel plate to create heat evenly. Ensure the pizza is not overcooked by using a lower temperature and checking it frequently. Avoid cramming the pizza into the oven, and consider using a cast iron skillet for better heat distribution. [4]
units.sources:
[1] How long should I bake the pizza in a microwave oven? (cited)
Tags: baking, pizza, microwave, convection I am making homemade pizza using a store bought pizza base. I know this is a fairly basic problem, but I am new here. Anyway, I own a Samsung microwave oven which also has a convection mode.

[2] homemade pizza - getting the dough crispy
Answers > Answer (score 2): I have worked on getting my crust really crispy and have found the following steps have really worked. Just an FYI, I use a pizza stone so my tip assumes you have a pizza stone. I put the pizza stone on the middle rack of my oven. Preheat your oven with the pizza stone inside the oven to the highest temperature it goes up to (mine reaches 525F).

[3] homemade pizza - getting the dough crispy
Answers > Answer (score 2): 4. Take the crust out of the oven and add the sauce, cheese, and toppings to the crust. Put the pizza back in the oven, cook for 3-4 minutes, turn the pizza 180 degrees, and cook another 3-4 minutes. This should really crisp up your pizza!!!

[4] How long should I bake the pizza in a microwave oven? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 6, accepted): Convection simply moves air around to heat evenly. I don't suggest cooking pizza in a microwave oven at all. If you don't want to use a conventional oven I would suggest trying to cook the pizza on a cast iron skillet instead. The secret to pizza is to cook as hot and quickly as possible, both top and bottom. This is more difficult to achieve in a pan, but if you're using store-bought pizza I would try cooking at a lower temperature with a lid on the pan to create a mini oven. If you have a blowtorch you can cook at a high temp and torch the top. Remember that cast iron heats really unevenly, so in either case leave the pan on the stove for a while to heat to temp evenly before you start the cook.

[5] How long should I bake the pizza in a microwave oven? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 4): If all you have is a convection microwave to cook with and the choice is microwave or convection mode then do convection mode as it's closer to baking. Microwaving a pizza will most likely turn it into overcooked rubber, convection gives you a chance. It's a good idea to cut the pizza into manageable chunks that the oven mode can handle, don't cram it in.

I've been in a situation where a microwave was all I have for cooking, I found that I was better off making foods that were microwave friendly rather than trying to cook things that weren't. Try your pizza in convection, if you get an acceptable result it opens up other options to you.

units.question: When a recipe says to bring the pot to a boil, which stage of bubbling counts?
units.gold: Tiny bubbles that sit on the bottom early on are just dissolved air leaving the water and do not count. A steady stream of small bubbles rising to the surface is a simmer. A boil is when the surface is clearly disturbed by bubbles, and a vigorous, churning boil is a rolling (roiling) boil. Remember that adding food drops the temperature, so judge by what you are cooking.
rubric: Says early bottom bubbles are dissolved air, not a simmer
Defines simmer as steady rising small bubbles
Defines boil as a disturbed surface and rolling boil as vigorous
Penalize: calling the first tiny bubbles a boil
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
When a recipe says to bring the pot to a boil, the stage of bubbling that counts is when the water starts to make bubbles, which is the first appearance of small bubbles on the surface. This is different from a simmer, which is a lower temperature, gentle bubbling. The boiling point of water is 100°C, but the actual temperature of the water can vary depending on factors like altitude and the presence of impurities. The key is to monitor the bubbling and reduce the heat once the water starts to boil.
units.sources:
[1] Should bubbles be forming only in center of pot when simmering? (Dutch oven on gas burner)
Tags: sauce, slow-cooking, dutch-oven I'm cooking Marcella Hazan's bolognese/ragu recipe using a brand new Le Creuset 7-quart round dutch oven. For the long simmering stage, the recipe says to keep the heat very low, which is what I'm doing. I'm noticing that the bubbles are appearing only at the very center of the pot (presumably because the flame is so small).

[2] At what point is water considered "at a boil?"
Answers > Answer (score 14): One important note is that while bringing water to a boil, there is first a point where a bunch of little bubbles form on the bottom of the pot. These initial bubbles are dissolved air coming out of solution as the water heats. The initial bubbles will occur at much lower temperatures, and long before the water simmers/boils. So, to add to BobMcGee's answer, 0 is bubbles forming on the bottom - not a simmer, 1 - small bubbles rising towards the surface is a simmer, 2 is a boil, 3 is a rolling boil.

[3] What does "bring to a simmer" mean?
Answers > Answer (score 17): "To simmer is to heat to a temperature point just off boiling, generally acknowledged as somewhere around 95 degrees C or something like 195 degrees F." - This statement is generally true. As noted above, if vapor bubbles are forming in a liquid, at least part of it is at its boiling point. units.question: Tell me how to cut and time garlic in a vegetable saute if I want the strongest garlic taste.
units.gold: Pungency is released by cutting, so the finer the cut the stronger: minced beats chopped, which beats sliced. Heat mellows the sharpness, and longer cooking makes garlic milder and sweeter as compounds break down. So mince it and add it near the end, about 30 seconds before the vegetables are done. Marinating ingredients with raw crushed garlic before a short cook also boosts the flavour.

States cooking mellows garlic, longer is milder/sweeter
Recommends adding minced garlic about 30 seconds before the end
Penalize: advising to fry garlic first for a long time for maximum pungency

[1] When should garlic be added to the pan to get maximum pungency?
Answers > Answer (score 6): Garlic's pungency is released by cutting it. The more finely the garlic is cut-up, the stronger its taste will be. So minced garlic will be stronger than chopped garlic. In order for garlic flavor to be strongest, you should mince the garlic and cook it briefly.

[2] Garlic bread
Garlic bread (also called garlic toast) consists of crusty bread slices topped with garlic and butter, and additional herbs such as oregano, chives or parsley. Garlic bread is typically made using a baguette, or sometimes ciabatta which is partially sliced downwards, allowing the condiments to soak into the loaf while keeping it in one piece. The bread is then stuffed through the cuts with oil and minced garlic before baking.

[3] How do I neutralize a strong garlic flavor?
Answers > Answer (score 4): If you didn't pre-roast your garlic and need to fix it after the fact... Throw your pesto in a saute pan with a little olive oil and cook it very lightly; that will help mellow the flavor. Also, are you using lemon juice in your garlic? Finally, make sure you are cutting out the "sprout" piece from the center of each garlic clove as that usually has the strongest, most unpleasant flavor.

[4] When should garlic be added to the pan to get maximum pungency?
Answers > Answer (score 2, accepted): Ana it really depends what sort of a dish you are making, and what texture and flavour you are after and the nature of garlic state: chopped, crushed, minced, pounded, etc.

If you want that pungent taste of garlic to be tasted, then you could add these crushed, chopped, sliced ones into your dish in the middle stage. If you do not want to taste too much of garlic, but just to go along, then minced ones are better and you may add a vee-bit at the earlier stage of the cooking. (I had to edit this passage as I had written it swapping the stages)

Garlic can be used for both oil based and water based dishes. Even for salads without oil! but with some flavours of lemon/lime and salt. We usually blend one raw garlic clove (as per the quantity) when making guacamole!!!

So are you sauteing vegetables? Or a gravy based dish? Should the dish go alone or with another set of course based dishes? =)

** Update as per OP's edit:---------- **

[5] When should garlic be added to the pan to get maximum pungency?
Answers > Answer (score 2, accepted): I must say it is quite rare to see chefs wanting to preserve the best pungent flavours of garlic/onions... ;)

Cooking the garlic by, say, roasting or frying it affects it in another way: its flavor changes as chemicals break down and reform into novel aromatic compounds. It also becomes sweeter as large sugars and carbohydrates break down into simpler sugars like fructose and glucose, both of which taste quite sweet to us.

The key to really great garlic flavor? Use a combination of techniques as indicated in the above article. Personally I like to do couple of things. Marinating with crushed/chopped/sliced garlic would be in your favour. The longer main-ingredients wrapped with raw garlic before cooking, the better they absorb the flavour as well as aroma. This only works for fast/short cooking dishes. Because longer cooking kills the pungency and makes the dish sweeter.

It all comes down to the chemistry of ingredients and heat - not to mention the experience you may get along!

units.question: Explain why ice cream recipes warm the dairy first and then cook it again after the egg yolks go in.
units.gold: Warming the milk, cream and sugar first dissolves the sugar fully, avoiding a gritty custard. Adding some warm dairy to the beaten yolks tempers them, raising their temperature gradually so they do not scramble when the rest goes in. The final heating cooks the custard to about 155-160 F, the minimum for eggs, without going higher. Mixing everything cold and heating at once can work for small batches, but for large batches the stepwise method is faster and less likely to scorch.
rubric: Explains warming dairy and sugar dissolves the sugar (smooth texture)
Explains tempering prevents scrambled yolks
Gives the final cooking target around 155-160 F
Notes all-at-once can work for small batches but is impractical for large ones
Penalize: claiming the two steps are purely tradition with no effect
units.answer: Ice cream recipes warm the dairy first to ensure it is at the right temperature, then cook it again with the egg yolks to thicken the base and create a smooth texture [4]. This process helps the dairy blend evenly with the yolks and achieves the desired consistency. The warming step ensures the dairy is not too cold, which would make it difficult to mix with the yolks. The cooking step thickens the mixture and enhances the flavor.

[1] Substitute for egg yolk in ice-cream (Egg Allergy)
Tags: substitutions, eggs, ice-cream, allergy I have a few questions regarding egg yolk in ice-cream. I would love to try making homemde ice-cream but a lot of recipes I see have egg yolk. What is the purpose of egg yolk in ice-cream?

[2] Ice cream technique - what should I mix into what?
Tags: ice-cream I have a homemade non-dairy ice cream recipe that involves a snow of egg whites and sugars, whip, and the egg yolks. At this point, the recipe says "mix together slowly with yolks". (That will ensure that the yolks don't sink to the bottom in the freezer :) )

[3] Ice cream
Ice cream is a frozen dessert typically made from milk or cream that has been flavoured with a sweetener, either sugar or an alternative, and a spice, such as cocoa or vanilla, or with fruit, such as strawberries or peaches. Food colouring is sometimes added in addition to stabilizers. The mixture is cooled below the freezing point of water and stirred to incorporate air spaces and prevent detectable ice crystals from forming. It can also be made by whisking a flavoured cream base and liquid nitrogen together.

[4] Can any custard be made into a frozen custard? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 8, accepted): There are a variety of frozen desserts which are all related. The main difference between ice cream and frozen custard is the amount of eggs used to thicken the base mix.

Philadelphia style ice cream is made from a base mix of milk and/or cream, sugar, and flavorings.

French (or simply plain) ice cream is made from a base mix which is essentially a very thin custard or creme anglaise: milk and/or cream, sugar, and flavorings thickened with egg yolks or whole egg. The base mix is cooked to thicken, and then chilled prior to churning.

Frozen custard is very similar to French style ice cream, but with a greater ratio of eggs or egg yolks to dairy or liquid in the mix.

With this information, you can adapt nearly any custard recipe to be freezable as ice cream or frozen custard.

My survey of frozen custard recipes indicates a ratio of eggs to dairy of about 5 egg yolks to three cups (700 mL) dairy, or 6 whole eggs to 4 cups (1 L) of dairy.

[5] Can any custard be made into a frozen custard? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 8, accepted): To adapt any custard recipe for freezing, then:

1.
Adjust the ratio of egg yolks to dairy to no more than about 5 yolks per 3 cups dairy.

You may also want to adjust the total yield to be based on no more than 3 cups dairy depending on the capacity of your ice cream maker. Many home ice cream makers have a 1 quart (close to 1 L) capacity, but you need to leave room for the air which will be incorporated as the mix is churned.

I recommend not using whole eggs for frozen custards, as the yolks facilitate a better texture, and create the rich eggy custard flavor.

2.
Frozen desserts are served colder than custards normally are, so the flavors will be more muted. You may need to compensate by increasing the ratio of flavoring ingredients.

This will be hard to judge until you have made the frozen custard/ice cream at least once.

3.
Cook the custard until it thickens on the stove top, per the normal custard method.

units.question: Does a lender looking at my credit report lower my score?
units.gold: It depends on the type of inquiry. A hard pull, made with your permission when you apply for credit, lowers your score a little, typically a few points for a while. A soft pull, used for pre-approved offers, background checks such as renting, or checking your own report, has no effect. Several similar hard pulls within a short shopping window (for example mortgage shopping over a couple of weeks) count only once. Hard pulls matter mainly when you are about to apply for a mortgage.
rubric: Distinguishes hard pulls (lower score) from soft pulls (no effect)
States the drop from a hard pull is small and temporary
Notes rate-shopping inquiries within a short window count once
Gives examples of soft pulls (pre-approved offers, own checks)
Penalize: claiming every check of the file lowers the score
units.answer: A lender looking at your credit report may lower your score if they find negative information, but they also consider your overall credit history [3]. The score is based on factors like payment history, credit utilization, and length of credit history. Lenders can pull from any of the three credit reports, and the score they use may vary slightly. It's best to check with the lender to understand which report they're using and how it affects your score.
units.sources:
[1] How to know which credit report / score will be consulted?
Answers > Answer (score 3): Your credit score is based on the information from your credit report. Since you have three different credit reports, you also have three potentially different credit scores from each credit score brand. For example, one lender may look at your FICO score based on your Equifax report, and another may look at your FICO score based on your Trans Union report. When you look at your credit score from a free source (such as Credit Karma), you are only given perhaps one score value.

[2] Credit rating
A credit rating is an evaluation of the credit risk of a prospective debtor (an individual, a business, company or a government). The credit rating represents an evaluation from a credit rating agency of the qualitative and quantitative information for the prospective debtor, including information provided by the prospective debtor and other non-public information obtained by the credit rating agency's analysts. Credit reporting (or credit score) is a subset of credit rating.

[3] Can I remove a legit negative from credit report? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 5, accepted): The credit file is a history of your use of credit. Now when you apply for credit the lender can decide to loan the money even if you don't have perfect credit. They may decide the risk is still good, or they could raise the rate, or they could lower the maximum they will lend. Some lenders will allow you to submit to them a written explanation of any ding on the report.

[4] How to know which credit report / score will be consulted?
I feel like I would get better chances of getting an additional credit card if I was applying to a credit card that was pulling my report from experian.

1. Am I right?
2. How can I know which report will be pulled by the institution I will apply to?

[5] How to know which credit report / score will be consulted?
Answers > Answer (score 1, accepted): I ... am trying to build a good credit score quickly.

You can't build a good credit score quickly. It takes time to prove that you will make payments on all of your credit accounts. Plus, activity that will be beneficial in the long term will hurt your score in the short term. In your case, it's probable that opening up new credit and taking out a car loan in a short period of time indicates that you have rapidly exceeded your spending, which makes you more of a credit risk, and going for a third card just compounds the problem.

How can I know which score will be pulled by the institution I will apply to?

You don't, and it shouldn't matter. Lenders can pull from any or all of the three providers, and they all should have roughly the same data. If there's a discrepancy or missing data that is causing them to give significantly different scores then you should contact them and sort out the discrepancies.

[6] How is an inquiry on the credit report different from checking credit score?
Answers > Answer (score 7, accepted): There are two types of inquiries when checking your credit score: soft and hard inquiries.

Soft inquiries usually do not affect your credit score. They can be triggered without your permission. Examples of soft inquiries are:

1. When you check your own credit score
2. When an employer checks your background/credit
3. When you get pre-approved for a credit card
4. Renting a car

Hard inquiries on the other hand affect your credit score. These are most likely triggered with your consent. They affect your credit score because if you trigger many hard inquiries; this is seen as being desperate for credit. Examples of hard inquiries are:

1. Getting a loan from your bank.
2. Applying for a credit card
3. Applying for a mortgage

units.question: I always settle my credit card statement the day it arrives instead of waiting for the due date. Am I losing anything?
units.gold: Very little. On a card with an interest-free grace period, paying early only forgoes the interest your cash could earn in savings until the due date; on a $2,000 monthly bill at 1% that is roughly $5 a year. One late payment would wipe out years of that gain through a late fee and interest, so paying early or setting autopay for the due date are both sensible. On a card with no interest-free period, paying sooner actually saves interest.

Notes that without a grace period early payment saves interest
Penalize: claiming early payment hurts the credit score

[1] Paying Credit Card statement amount in full on due date and using it in the same day
Tags: credit-card, credit-score, payment, balance I paid my Credit Card statement amount yesterday in full (which I always do), on due date. Immediately after an hour (before the transaction is even processed), I used the Credit Card for other purchases. However, for the past two months I am paying ON time, that increased my credit score by 10pts.

[2] Credit card billing cycles and due date
Answers > Answer (score 1): The statement date is the date that is the last date of transactions on each monthly statement. You are required to make a payment between the statement date and the due date that is at least the minimum payment. I recommend paying off your whole credit card balance in full each month. You can wait until you receive the monthly statement, and then instead of paying the minimum due, pay the full statement balance shown on the statement by the due date.

[3] If my credit card payment is due in 3 days time, will anything I order today have to be paid by then too?
Answers > Answer (score 14, accepted): If you're in the US - then no. You'll owe payment on your purchase on your next statement due date (September 12th), not your current due date (August 12th). In other countries, your closing date and due date may be the same, in which case you're required to make a payment on the same day your statement is posted. After your statement is posted on the closing date, you usually have a grace period of at least 21 days (since the passage of the Credit CARD Act of 2009) before you're required to make at least the minimum payment on the statement's balance and before interest begins accruing on your balance.

[4] If my credit card payment is due in 3 days time, will anything I order today have to be paid by then too?
Answers > Answer (score 14, accepted): Note that your balance before you make a payment may include the balance of your last statement and the balance of your purchases after the statement is posted, but if you select the option to pay in full, the amount you pay will be the balance of your last statement, not the total current balance on your card. In general, it's the balance when your statement is posted that matters. This varies depending on your credit card provider, but it's probably somewhere in the online interface, or you could call their customer service and ask them to change the date for you. Some credit card companies won't let you change this date during your card's anniversary period, so you may need to wait until the next period to change it.

[5] If my credit card payment is due in 3 days time, will anything I order today have to be paid by then too?
1. The Credit Card payment due date is the 12th of every month, and that applies to all of their customers. This date cannot be changed.
2. The payment due date has a grace-period of 10 days. Using the grace period has no attached penalty nor does it affect one's credit-rating. I asked if there was any reason not to use the grace period and they told me "no".
3. Charges made to the card between the 1st and 31st of Month 1 will require payment by the 12th of Month 2. Charges made to the card between the 1st and 31st of Month 2 will not require payment until the 12th of Month 3, not Month 2.

So that clears that up then :)

[6] Is there any drawback to paying credit card bills immediately rather than waiting until payment is due?
Answers > Answer (score 5, accepted): The math depends on your average bill, days before it's due, and interest you'd earn. Say you have a $2000 bill each month. At 1%, there's an annual $20 or 40 cents per week you'd save by delaying the payment. If you pay on line and can hit the due date dead on, no reason to pay sooner. But if you risk the mail being late, the late fee and interest will negate the savings on a hundred months of last minute payments. Hardly worth the risk, IMHO.

Edit - to clarify, the delayed payment with the above numbers saves the 40 cents or about $5/yr. scale it up with higher average balances or with a higher return on your savings account.

[7] Is there any drawback to paying credit card bills immediately rather than waiting until payment is due?
Answers > Answer (score 5): If you have a credit card with no interest free period, there is no drawback as you will be saving interest the sooner you pay it off.

However, if you have a credit card with an interest free period, the drawback on paying it earlier than the due date (such as when you first get the statement) is that you lose out on interest. For the period between when you first recieve the statement to when it is due, you could have your money earning you interest in a high interest paying savings account. Depending on how much you spend on your credit card each month and the interest rate you get, this may add up to quite a bit of additional cash each year.

units.question: To build credit, is it better to be added to a family member's premium card as an authorized user, or to open a secured card myself?
units.gold: Authorized-user status helps only if the issuer reports authorized users to the bureaus (not all do). If it does, your relative's on-time payments help you, but their missed payments or high utilisation can hurt you and you cannot control them. Your own secured card puts you in control and, if the issuer keeps the history when you upgrade to an unsecured card, builds length of credit. Being removed later can drop your score. The card's annual fee and perks do not affect the score.
rubric: Notes not all issuers report authorized users
Explains the relative's late payments or high utilisation can hurt you
Explains own card gives control and builds account history
States rewards or annual fee do not affect the score
Penalize: claiming a premium card's tier itself raises your score
units.answer: Being added as an authorized user to a family member's premium card can help build credit, as it adds your name to the credit history. However, opening a secured credit card yourself may offer more control and better long-term benefits. Secured cards require a deposit and can help build credit through timely payments, but they may have lower limits and fees [3]. Ultimately, both options can help, but a secured card may be more effective for building credit initially.
units.sources:
[1] Improving my credit score by getting my own card vs being added as an authorized user on a better card (cited)
Tags: credit-card, credit-score Does getting added as an authorized user on my relative's higher tier credit card (with an annual fee and better benefits) have a different impact on my credit score when compared to getting my own secured credit card?

[2] Will Adding myself as a co-holder of my parent's credit card build my credit history?
Answers > Answer (score 2): Yes it will help your credit history if you are added to your parents credit card as an authorized user, the card will show up on your credit history as if you got the card when they opened the account originally. Technically authorized user is a loophole that FICO claims to have fixed in the past but I don't think they actually have. I am also assuming that you and your parents are in the US and the credit card account is from a US bank. Your real problem though is the fact you don't have any income without income you are going to have a very hard time getting a credit card.

[3] Improving my credit score by getting my own card vs being added as an authorized user on a better card (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 2): Your own personal credit card would be better, IMHO, since you won't depend on someone else's behavior. While having a higher tier card means they're probably reasonably disciplined, it's still a risk. On the other hand secured card requires a deposit and will come with lower credit limit and potentially fees, but that's temporary and may not be such a bad thing if you're just starting building your credit.

[4] Which is better to build credit score? Becoming an authorized user of another credit card or get a personal secured credit card?
Tags: united-states, credit-card, credit-score, credit-history, secured-credit-card I am new to the US with a F-2(student dependent) visa, I want to have credit history and build credit score in the US. Apply for a secured credit card with $500-1000 deposit in few banks who don't need SSN/ITIN(like Bank of America) and get a secured credit card(I think it gonna take less than 1 week). 3- Become an authorized user of the credit card of another person like my wife, she has SSN and regular credit card.

[5] Improving my credit score by getting my own card vs being added as an authorized user on a better card (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 2, accepted): Many credit card companies report authorized users to credit bureaus, but not all do. If they don't, your credit won't be impacted by being an authorized user. Check with your relative's card company to be sure. But assuming being an authorized user does go on your credit report:

Your credit can be positively impacted by continued on-time payment history by your relative. However, if they miss a payment, your credit could be harmed even though they (as the primary cardholder) are solely responsible for making payments.

High utilization of the card (as a percentage of the limit) can also hurt your credit, although this is generally much more temporary since reducing utilization has a pretty immediate positive impact. However, you won't be able to control the utilization percentage as an authorized user the same way you would as the primary or only cardholder.

[6] Improving my credit score by getting my own card vs being added as an authorized user on a better card (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 2, accepted): In the long term, having your own card could have a more positive impact if your credit card company retains your account history when you eventually switch from a secured to an unsecured card. Length of credit is a substantial portion of your score. On the flip side, if you're removed as an authorized user on someone else's card, you may see a drop in credit score when the credit history drops off of your report (generally 10 years after closing).

The annual fee and better benefits (miles, perks, cashback rewards, etc.) shouldn't impact your score.

units.question: Tell me how to get a refund check payable to me and my former roommate deposited when we now live in different cities.
units.gold: A check made out to both of you ("and") generally needs both endorsements, and a bank may refuse to deposit it into an account in only one name, so call the depositing bank first. Easier options: ask the landlord to reissue it as two checks for half each, or to make it payable "and/or"; or one of you endorses it "For Deposit Only", deposits it (an ATM deposit is less hassle) and pays the other their share separately.
rubric: Notes both endorsements are usually needed for an "and" check
Advises checking with the bank where it will be deposited
Suggests asking the landlord to reissue as two checks or "and/or"
Mentions depositing it and paying the roommate separately
Penalize: telling one person to sign the other's name
units.answer:
The passages found don't support this answer. From the model's memory, may be wrong:
If a check is payable to you and your former roommate and deposited when you now live in different cities, you can contact the bank where the check was issued to request a refund. The bank may need information about the account holder and the current address to process the refund. If the check was made out to both of you, you can request a duplicate check or a refund based on the original check. If the check was made out to one of you, you can contact the bank to request the refund for the other person. You may need to provide proof of identity and the current address to facilitate the refund process.

[1] How can I deposit a check made out to my business into my personal account?
Answers > Answer (score 4): For-profit operations are similar; an apartment complex may get checks payable to the apartment name, the management company name, even the landlord. I expect that your freelance work will be no different.

[2] If a check is made payable to my son c/o me but mailed to my son, can he deposit it into his own account without my endorsement?
Tags: endorsement Not sure why but my son received a refund at his house that is payble to him c/o me. Can he deposit without my endorsement?

[3] If a check is made payable to my son c/o me but mailed to my son, can he deposit it into his own account without my endorsement?
Answers > Answer (score 5): Yes, your son can deposit or cash the check. c/o is merely a direction to the mailman as to where to deliver the envelope and doesn’t give you any rights to the money.

[4] Victim of a Vacation Rental Scam, how should I get the refund?
Answers > Answer (score 2): If you paid paid by credit card, this is relatively easy: Dispute the payment with your bank.

Some banks have this built into their app or online banking, with others you need to write them to dispute the charge. You may have to give a brief explanation on why you're disputing the payment, but you don't have to submit any documentation.

The way these things work the bank will "charge back" the money into your account, and if the merchant wants it back they will have to submit proof that the transaction was actually valid. Which is very unlikely in this case, if they scammed more than just you the account will already be under investigation.

Some banks require you to make a report to the police, though, if criminal activity is involved.

If you paid directly to booking.com, you may ask them to revert the transaction; but if they don't react quickly still dispute the payment.

Don't delay too long, as has been noted in the other answer, there's limited time to charge back your money.

[5] How to enforce receipt or contract for renting the holiday's apartment in Israel?
Answers > Answer (score 3, accepted): Reach out to your financial department, describe the situation, and ask for guidance. They might give you a leeway, or accept your ATM receipt as evidence. After all if you spent several days in the city on business, and didn't submit any lodging expenses, it is obvious you didn't sleep on the street - so the accounting might be able to get this through.

PS. The people most likely are trying to avoid taxes, which is easy since you paid in cash.

units.question: Why do ordinary US bank transfers and direct deposits take a business day or more to clear?
units.gold: Because they run on the Automated Clearing House (ACH) network, which collects transactions during the day and settles them in a batch at the end of each business day. In the batch, banks net out what they owe each other, so instead of moving money for every individual payment, only the differences change hands, which turns many transactions into a few inter-bank transfers. If you need money moved faster, use a wire transfer, which costs an extra fee.
rubric: Names ACH and batch processing at the end of each business day
Explains netting: only the differences between banks move
Mentions wire transfer as the faster, paid alternative
Penalize: attributing the delay only to fraud checks
units.answer: Ordinary US bank transfers and direct deposits take a business day or more to clear because these transactions are processed in batches at the end of each business day [1]. The ACH network accumulates transactions and processes them collectively, which delays the clearing of individual transfers. This delay is consistent with banking regulations that require funds to be available the business day after the transaction date. The delay is not due to the system itself but rather bank policies and the way transactions are processed in batches.
units.sources:
[1] Why do (ACH) payments that withdraw or deposit on my bank account require 1+ business days to complete? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 4): Automated Clearing House transactions are used in the US for direct deposit of pay checks and direct debit of many payments for accounts such as mortgages, credit cards, car loans, insurance premiums, etc. The reason they take one or more business days to clear is that the transactions are accumulated by each processor in the network during the day and processed as a batch at the end of each business day. The ACH network processes 20+ billion transactions per year worth $40 trillion, (estimates based on 2012 figures).

[2] How can a bank make it possible for their customers to get their salary up to two days in advance?
Answers > Answer (score 13): This policy is standard for many US banks, e.g. Wells Fargo and Chase and often applies to all ACH/direct deposits, such as government benefits, pensions, and tax refunds. Normal ACH/direct deposit clears overnight on business days. The bank receives a message that money is to be deposited, but the actual fund transfers are netted. Consistent with this clearing, by law, the bank must make the money available the business day after the business day on which ACH transaction arrives.

[3] Why do transfers between your own accounts WITHIN the same bank take a business day to clear?
Tags: banking, money-transfer Why is it that when you e.g. transfer money between your savings and checking account at a bank in the U.S. (say Bank of America), it takes a business day for the transaction to clear? I understand why this would be the case for inter-bank transfers, but I don't understand why this is the case for intra-bank transfers.

[4] How can a bank make it possible for their customers to get their salary up to two days in advance?
Answers > Answer (score 13): (Same-day direct deposit/ACH exists. Basically the same process occurs several times throughout the day. The employer has to be so motivated to elect for it, the bank loses the float on the money and therefore charges the employer more for the service.)

In most cases, therefore the bank advances you money for a matter of hours. Two days early occurs if you are paid on Friday, like many people are, then funds normally become available on Monday, and here the bank makes it available on Friday.

If you use those funds for a delayed clearing transaction, like an outgoing ACH (bill/mortgage payment), check clearing, or debit card purchase, the bank will have the funds in hand before they are sent out again. Only transactions like cash withdrawals and wires will the bank actually have to loan you funds.

The bank loses a little on float (interest) but gains customer loyalty and use of the account as one's default deposit account.

[5] Why do transfers between your own accounts WITHIN the same bank take a business day to clear?
Answers > Answer (score 6, accepted): That depends on your bank. My credit union clears intra-account transfers immediately. The delay therefore is based on bank policy.

It is possible that in the system the accounts are not really linked and so it treats transfers between accounts that you own and accounts between people the same. And further in the case of your bank that they decided to have s one day hold. I believe that'll have heard some banks advertise that you can electronically transfer money to another account holder at the same bank in just 15 min.

I would also make sure that you are selecting immediate transfer instead of a future date transfer. Mine has those as two different options and if you select the other, you just select the date of action to be at least one in the future.

The ACH network processes 20+ billion transactions per year worth $40 trillion, (estimates based on 2012 figures).

units.question: What stops American credit unions from accepting any customer who walks in?
units.gold: Federal law. 12 USC 1759(b) limits credit union membership to groups sharing a common bond (an employer, an organisation, a community) or to people in a particular area, and each charter states who may join. Credit unions are member-owned, not-for-profit institutions with preferential tax and regulatory treatment; the limits exist so they do not compete too freely with banks, which oppose loosening them. Credit unions would like looser rules but not at the cost of their tax advantages.
rubric: Cites the legal requirement of a common bond or geographic area
Explains credit unions are member-owned not-for-profit institutions
Explains the limits offset their tax advantages so banks stay competitive
Penalize: claiming it is merely each credit union's marketing choice
units.answer: American credit unions are mutually-owned financial institutions that provide banking services [1]. They take deposits from their members (customers) and loan them to other members [1]. Members vote on a board of directors who manage operations [1]. State-chartered credit unions don't have to maintain deposit insurance at all [1].

Answers > Answer (score 12, accepted): For any online service that is prepaid by the month or other period, like Major League Baseball live streaming (annually), Netflix (monthly) etc., it is impossible for the merchant to dispute the chargeback. If the customer doesn't want your service, stop selling it to them and walk away. Answers > Answer (score 27, accepted): Please realize that your issuer can close the account for any number of reasons. I have a credit card issued by my credit union that I have not used for a couple of years. If I were not an otherwise profitable customer, I wouldn't be surprised if they closed my credit card account.

Answers > Answer (score 15, accepted): Other organizations with similar limits have gone on to be competitive when the limits were released. For example, there used to be an insurance company just for government employees, the Government Employees Insurance Company. You may know it better as GEICO (yes, the one with the gecko advertisements). Now they offer life and auto insurance all over.

Credit unions would like looser limitations (or no limitations at all), but not enough to give up their preferential tax treatment. Banks oppose looser limitations and have as much political clout as credit unions.

[5] How do I insist that American hotels accept my employer's credit card for payment, instead of asking for personal credit card upon check-in?
Answers > Answer (score 21): We ended up solving this problem by opening a corporate account with the hotel chain, which was specifically designed to handle precisely these sorts of bookings. Not only is the problem now solved, but we also get discounted rates and interest free credit from the hotel, together with itemised monthly billing by cost centre. I guess this is something that most the big chains offer, but for what it’s worth the programme we enrolled with is Business Advantage from IHG. An added benefit of their scheme is that the person making the booking receives Business Rewards points whilst the guest staying in the hotel still receives their own Rewards Club points as normal (and if the two happen to be the same person, bonus points!).

units.question: I am moving a pre-tax 401(k) from an old job. Can it go into a Roth IRA, and which destination makes more sense?
units.gold: You can, but money moved from a pre-tax 401(k) into a Roth is taxed as a conversion. A common approach is to roll it into a traditional IRA first (no tax now) and then convert to Roth in chunks that fill your current tax bracket. Choose Roth if you expect a higher tax rate in retirement than now, traditional if lower. An IRA usually offers more investment choices and lower fees than a 401(k), though a 401(k) allows penalty-free withdrawals after separating at 55.
rubric: States a Roth destination is possible but triggers tax as a conversion
Recommends traditional IRA and optional partial conversions
Ties the choice to current vs expected retirement tax rate
Mentions IRA's broader options/lower fees versus 401(k)
Penalize: claiming a pre-tax 401(k) cannot be moved to a Roth at all
units.answer: A pre-tax 401(k) can be converted to a Roth IRA without being 59.5 or leaving the job [1]. Rolling it into a Roth IRA offers tax-free withdrawals in the future, but the conversion is taxable [4]. A traditional IRA may be a better option for current tax purposes, as it avoids the conversion tax. Choosing a Roth IRA is generally better for long-term wealth accumulation. The best destination depends on your current financial situation and future tax expectations.

The contributions can go into a Roth and the earnings go into a pre-tax account.

Can a Roth 401(k) be rolled over / in-service distributed / transferred somehow to a Roth IRA if younger than 59.5-year-old and not leaving one's job?

[4] Can one roll over an after-tax 401(k) to a Roth IRA, then any time in the future withdraw my contributions tax-free and penalty-free? (cited)
Tags: united-states, 401k, roth-ira, roth-conversion, penalty Background information: in the United States, traditional (a.k.a. pre-tax)/Roth/after-tax (a.k.a. post-tax) 401(k) may be rolled over as follows: - A traditional 401(k) may be rolled over to a traditional IRA or Roth IRA if older than 59.5-year-old or if leaving one's job. - A Roth 401(k) may be rolled over to a Roth IRA if older than 59.5-year-old or if leaving one's job.

[5] Conflicting advice about what to do with my 401k / Roth IRA
I do know that when I take the contributions out they will be taxed. I also know that if I do move them into my Roth IRA they will be taxed since Roth IRA's are after tax contributions. I also know that right now I have no plans whatsoever to actually cash my old account in and pay all these fees plus taxes - I do not need the money.

Is there a preferred option you would take or what am I missing here?

[6] Conflicting advice about what to do with my 401k / Roth IRA
Answers > Answer (score 7, accepted): Have you considered the alternative of rolling over your 401(k) to a brand-new Traditional IRA instead of into your already-established Roth IRA? Such a rollover (to a Traditional IRA) would not incur any taxes now and you would save the annual fees that you are being charged for the 401(k) plan of your previous employer. Most IRA custodians waive the annual maintenance fee charged to IRA accounts when the IRA assets rise above a certain level ($10K? $25K?) and if your chosen IRA custodian is unwilling to waive the fee when you are proposing to roll over $500K, it is time to find another IRA custodian. In contrast, 401(k) plan providers don't often waive their fees; they have a captive audience who can't go elsewhere.

[7] Move money from former employer's 401k to Roth IRA and Rollover IRA
Answers > Answer (score 7, accepted): Yes, it is. Your 401k plan at Vanguard is required to differentiate between pre-tax contributions and earnings, Roth contributions, and Roth earnings. When you request a rollover, you'll designate an account for the pre-tax money to go into, and you'll designate a different account for the Roth contributions and Roth earnings to go into. If you're going to direct the pre-tax money to a Rollover IRA at Fidelity, you'd most likely direct the Roth contributions and Roth earnings to a Roth IRA at Fidelity.

This rollover chart from the IRS details where you can roll different accounts to. In your case, 30% is a qualified plan (pre-tax) and 70% is a designated Roth account. You can roll your pre-tax money into a Roth account, but be aware that rolling pre-tax money to a Roth account is a taxable event. You can't roll Roth money into a pre-tax account.

units.question: Since 401(k) withdrawals are taxed as ordinary income rather than at the lower capital-gains rate, is a regular brokerage account the better deal?
units.gold: Usually not, because the comparison is not like for like. Money for a taxable account has already been taxed as income before you invest it, and then you also pay tax on dividends and capital gains. With a flat 20% rate, $10,000 in a traditional 401(k) growing tenfold leaves $80,000 after tax, the same as a Roth, while the taxable account nets less. Employer matching makes the 401(k) even better. Taxable accounts do win on liquidity and investment choice.
rubric: Explains taxable investing uses after-tax money and is taxed again on gains/dividends
Shows deferral gives the same result as Roth at constant rates, better than taxable
Mentions the employer match
Acknowledges liquidity or fund choice as valid reasons for taxable accounts
Penalize: concluding the taxable account is better just because the capital gains rate is lower
units.answer: A regular brokerage account is generally better for long-term gains because it allows you to benefit from the lower capital gains tax rate when holding investments for more than a year [2]. However, if you sell investments within a year, they are taxed as ordinary income, which is higher [4]. The choice depends on your holding period and tax situation.
units.sources:
[1] Short Term Capital Gains tax vs. IRA Withdrawal Tax w/o Quarterly Est. Taxes
Answers > Answer (score 3): (In fact, there may be a difference. As you note, you will pay tax at the capital gains rate on gains from selling in a taxable account. But if you sell the stocks inside the IRA and withdraw, that is ordinary income. However, since ordinary income is taxed at a higher rate than long-term capital gains, you will potentially pay more tax on the IRA withdrawal, since it will be taxed at the higher rate, if your gains are long-term rather than short term.

[2] What retirement accounts are available without age based withdrawal penalties? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 13): 3. There's a tax benefit in long term investing in a regular taxable brokerage accounts - long term capital gains are taxed at a preferable (lower) rate than short term or ordinary income. The condition here is holding an investment for more than a year, and there's no penalty for not satisfying it but there's a reward (lower rates) if you do.

[3] Post Tax 401k or Taxable Brokerage Account?
Answers > Answer (score 5): A post-tax IRA is not a very good deal. If you invest in a brokerage account instead, you pay capital gains taxes when you sell. I don't have a reference but I don't think the long-term capital gains rate has ever been higher than the ordinary income rate in the same bracket, and for as long as I can remember, it has often been a lot lower. Short term capital gains are at worst taxed at ordinary income rates.

[4] What is the benefit of investing in retirement plan versus investing directly in stocks yourself? (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 3): In the US, the key to understanding the benefits of retirement accounts is to understand capital gains taxes and how they work. Retirement accounts are designed for making investments throughout your career, then after several decades of contributions, withdrawing that money to pay for your needs when your full-time employment has concluded. Normally when you invest money in a brokerage account, if the value of your investment increases, and you sell in less than a year, those investments are considered short-term gains and taxed as ordinary income. If you hold that same investment for over a year, the same investment is taxed at a lower capital gains rate (depending on which tax bracket you are in during that year, the amount due could be up to 20%, but much lower than your regular income tax rate).

[5] Post Tax 401k or Taxable Brokerage Account?
AFTER TAX EE DEFERRALS The amount you can contribute to a retirement savings plan, using a portion of your salary that has already been included in your taxable income. Income taxes have already been calculated on the amount contributed. However, any earnings on these contributions can grow tax-deferred. Income taxes are not due on any earnings until they are withdrawn from the plan. Your company may match all or a portion of your after-tax contributions in order to provide them with the most flexibility regarding taxes. (It may be advantageous for some people to pay taxes on the contributions now, because they would be in a higher tax bracket during retirement).

[6] Post Tax 401k or Taxable Brokerage Account?
Answers > Answer (score 7, accepted): With my additional savings is there any reason i would want to do a post-tax 401k instead of keeping it in a regular taxable brokerage account?

Let's clarify what you mean by "post-tax 401k".

First there is the Roth 401k, which behaves like a Roth IRA -- money that you contribute is taxed, but you pay no taxes on earnings when you withdraw them in retirement. However, a Roth 401k shares the same contribution pool as a Traditional 401k, so if your goal is to invest more money, this is not helpful -- every dollar you contribute to a Roth 401k is one less dollar you can contribute to a Traditional 401k, and vice versa.

[7] Individual retirement account
An individual retirement account or IRA is a form of "individual retirement plan". It is simply a savings account with large tax advantages. An IRA is not itself an investment. It is where an investor keeps assets such as stocks, bonds and mutual funds. A 401(k) is set up by an employer, but an IRA may be started by an individual. Other IRAs may be opened by small business owners and those who are self-employed.

units.question: My high-deductible plan and HSA both started on January 1. Can I still put money in for the prior tax year before the April filing deadline?
units.gold: No. Prior-year contributions are allowed only if you were HSA-eligible (covered by a high-deductible plan) during that year. If your HDHP coverage started this January, your prorated limit for last year is zero and the last-month rule does not apply. Had you been covered last year and only opened the account late, you could contribute for that year until the April deadline. If you had an HDHP for part of last year, the limit is reduced proportionally.
rubric: States contributions for a year require HDHP eligibility in that year
Concludes the prior-year limit is zero here
Explains late opening is fine if you were eligible that year
Mentions proration for partial-year coverage or the last-month rule
Penalize: saying any contribution before April 15 counts for the prior year
units.answer: You can make HSA contributions for the prior tax year even if the account started on January 1, as long as you open the account before the April 15 deadline [2]. The IRS allows contributions for the previous tax year even if the account was established later. The contribution limit is determined by the tax year in question [4]. If you have an HDHP, you can contribute to the HSA for the prior tax year [2].

units.question: Walk me through how vested restricted stock units are taxed, including what happens when I later sell the shares.
units.gold: RSUs are taxed as salary when they vest, on their value at that moment; brokers often sell part of the shares to cover the withholding. That vest-date value becomes your cost basis. From then on they are an ordinary stock position: selling within a year of vesting gives short-term gains, after more than a year long-term. Each vesting lot has its own date and basis, so you calculate gains per lot. Holding vested RSUs is economically like receiving cash and buying the stock.
rubric: States RSUs are taxed as ordinary income at vesting on their value
Explains the vest-date value is the cost basis
Explains short vs long-term depends on holding more than a year after vesting
Notes each lot is tracked separately
Penalize: saying the basis is the grant-date value or that RSUs get capital gains treatment at vest
units.answer: When vested restricted stock units are sold, the tax treatment depends on the sale price and the cost basis. The gain is calculated as the selling price minus the cost basis, which is the price at which you acquired the shares. The gain is taxed at your ordinary income tax rate. If you sell the shares before they vest, the tax is based on the fair market value at the time of sale. If you sell after vesting, the tax is based on the cost basis. The proceeds are reported on your tax return, and the gain is subject to capital gains tax [2].

[2] Restricted Stock Grants - How to prepare tax return when you sell to cover taxes (cited)
Answers > Answer (score 2, accepted): You don't. When you sell them - your cost basis would be the price of the stock at which you sold the stocks to cover the taxes, and the difference is your regular capital gain.

[3] What will happen to my restricted units?
Answers > Answer (score 2, accepted): This should all be covered in your stock grant documentation, or the employee stock program of which your grant is a part. Find those docs and it should specify how or when you can sale your shares, and how the money is paid to you. Generally, vested shares are yours until you take action. If instead you have options, then be aware these need to be exercised before they become shares. There is generally a limited time period on how long you can wait to exercise. In the US, 10 years is common.

Unvested shares will almost certainly expire upon your departure of the company. Whether your Merrill Lynch account will show this, or show them as never existing, I can't say. But either way, there is nothing you can or should do.

[4] Capital gains tax
A capital gains tax is a tax on the profit realized on the sale of a non-inventory asset. The most common capital gains are seen from the sale of stocks, bonds, precious metals, real estate, and property.

Not all countries have a capital gains tax and most have different rates of taxation. Countries that do not impose a capital gains tax include Bahrain, Barbados, Belize, Cayman Islands, Isle of Man, Jamaica, New Zealand, Sri Lanka, Singapore, and others.

In some countries, such as New Zealand and Singapore, professional traders and those who trade frequently are taxed on such profits as a business income.

In the United Kingdom people paid £16.7 billion in capital gains tax in 2021-22.
